+import { test, beforeEach } from "node:test"
+import assert from "node:assert/strict"
+import { reset, db } from "../src/store.js"
+import { createAccount, deleteAccount } from "../src/accounts.js"
+import { issueInvoice } from "../src/invoices.js"
+import { runDaily } from "../src/jobs.js"
+import { createServer } from "../src/server.js"
+
+beforeEach(reset)
+
+const DAY = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+const issuedAt = new Date("2020-03-15T12:00:00Z")
+const sevenYearsLater = new Date("2027-03-15T12:00:00Z")
+const lines = [{ description: "Brand workshop", quantity: 1, unitPrice: 45000 }]
+
+function erasedInvoice() {
+  const user = createAccount({ name: "Ada Park", email: "ada@studio.example", address: "1 Loom Lane, London" })
+  const invoice = issueInvoice(user.id, lines, { taxId: "GB123456789", now: issuedAt })
+  deleteAccount(user.id)
+  return invoice
+}
+
+test("an erased invoice is kept until 7 years after its issue date", () => {
+  const invoice = erasedInvoice()
+  runDaily(new Date(sevenYearsLater - DAY))
+  assert.equal(db.invoices.has(invoice.id), true)
+})
+
+test("an erased invoice past 7 years is purged and the purge is audited", () => {
+  const invoice = erasedInvoice()
+  const now = new Date(sevenYearsLater.getTime() + DAY)
+  runDaily(now)
+  assert.equal(db.invoices.has(invoice.id), false)
+  const entries = db.audit.filter((entry) => entry.action === "invoice.purged")
+  assert.deepEqual(entries, [{
+    at: now.toISOString(),
+    action: "invoice.purged",
+    subject: invoice.id,
+    detail: { kinds: ["billing"], rule: "invoice-retention-7y" },
+  }])
+})
+
+test("a live account's invoice is never purged", () => {
+  const user = createAccount({ name: "Bea Moss", email: "bea@studio.example" })
+  const invoice = issueInvoice(user.id, lines, { now: issuedAt })
+  runDaily(new Date("2028-03-15T12:00:00Z"))
+  assert.equal(db.invoices.has(invoice.id), true)
+})
+
+test("the server runs the daily jobs when it starts", async () => {
+  const longAgo = new Date("2015-06-01T12:00:00Z")
+  const ada = createAccount({ name: "Ada Park", email: "ada@studio.example", address: "1 Loom Lane, London" })
+  const erased = issueInvoice(ada.id, lines, { now: longAgo })
+  deleteAccount(ada.id)
+  const bea = createAccount({ name: "Bea Moss", email: "bea@studio.example" })
+  const live = issueInvoice(bea.id, lines, { now: longAgo })
+
+  const server = createServer()
+  await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, resolve))
+  server.close()
+

+# Account erasure
+
+## Interface
+
+`src/erasure.js` exports `eraseAccount(user, now = new Date())`.
+
+It reads and writes `db` directly, as `src/jobs.js` does. Because it imports
+only `src/store.js` and `src/audit.js`, it avoids an accounts↔invoices import
+cycle.
+
+`deleteAccount(userId, now)` in `src/accounts.js` keeps its signature. It
+looks up the live account, calls `eraseAccount(user, now)` and returns
+`true`. For an unknown id it returns `false`, as today.
+
+## Behaviour
+
+In this order:
+
+1. Capture `user.email` (step 5 needs it once the account record is gone).
+2. Delete every `db.sessions` entry whose `userId` matches. This is the
+   existing loop, moved here.
+3. Remove every `db.events` item whose `userId` matches.
+4. Delete every `db.tickets` entry whose `userId` matches.
+5. `db.subscribers.delete(email)`.
+6. For every `db.invoices` entry whose `userId` matches, minimise it per
+   [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-invoice-minimisation-and-retention.md).
+7. For those invoices, delete `detail.userId` from their `invoice.issued`
+   audit entries.
+8. Delete the `db.users` entry.
+9. Write the `account.erased` entry per
+   [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-erasure-audit-entry.md). This replaces the current
+   `account.deleted` entry.
+
+## Related changes
+
+- `src/server.js`: `DELETE /me` stops calling
+  `track(user, "account.delete_requested")`. Step 3 would erase that event,
+  so it only puts a copy of the email in `db.events` for a moment.
+- `src/accounts.js`: drop `deletedAt` from the created user and its checks
+  in `createAccount`, `findAccount` and `signIn`.
+
+## Invariants after `eraseAccount`
+
+- No store has the account's email, phone, or free-text ticket content.
+- No store has the userId, except as the subject of audit entries.
+- Every invoice the account had still has `id`, `issuedAt`, `lines`,
+  `total`, `billing.name`, `billing.address`, `billing.taxId`.
+- Other accounts' data is unchanged.

+# 0001 Erase at deletion
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted.
+
+## Context
+
+Personal data must be erased within 30 days of account deletion. Today
+`deleteAccount` only sets `deletedAt` and removes sessions. A flagged record
+is not erased. Every store is in process memory (`src/store.js`), so erasure
+needs no external calls.
+
+## Decision
+
+`deleteAccount` erases the account's personal data in the same call, through
+`eraseAccount` ([spec](../spec/account-erasure.md)). The `db.users` entry is
+removed, not flagged. Since nothing then sets `deletedAt`, the field and its
+checks in `createAccount`, `findAccount` and `signIn` are removed.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- The 30-day limit is met at once, with no pending state and no job to
+  monitor.
+- Deletion cannot be undone. Nothing asks for a grace period or undo, so none
+  is built.
+- `DELETE /me` and `deleteAccount` keep their current signatures and
+  responses.

+# Invoice retention purge
+
+## Interface
+
+`src/jobs.js` adds `purgeExpiredInvoices(now)` to `dailyJobs`, next to
+`expireSessions`. `runDaily(now)` runs it.
+
+## Behaviour
+
+For every `db.invoices` entry with `erasedAt` set, compute its expiry as
+`issuedAt` plus 7 calendar years (`setUTCFullYear(year + 7)`). If that
+expiry is before `now`:
+
+1. delete the invoice from `db.invoices`;
+2. write `record("invoice.purged", invoice.id, { kinds: ["billing"], rule: "invoice-retention-7y" }, now)`
+   per [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-erasure-audit-entry.md).
+
+Invoices without `erasedAt`, which belong to live accounts, are never
+purged by this job.
+
+## Checks
+
+- Erased invoice, 7 years minus 1 day after `issuedAt`: kept.
+- Erased invoice, 7 years plus 1 day after `issuedAt`: deleted, one
+  `invoice.purged` entry.
+- Live account's invoice, 8 years after `issuedAt`: kept.

+# 0003 Erasure audit entry
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted.
+
+## Context
+
+Each erasure must be recorded in the audit log: what kind of data was
+erased, when, and under which rule, never the erased values. The existing
+`invoice.issued` entry stores `detail.userId`, a second copy of the
+invoice→account link that [ADR 0002](0002-invoice-minimisation-and-retention.md)
+removes from the invoice.
+
+## Decision
+
+- Account erasure writes one entry:
+  `record("account.erased", userId, { kinds, rule: "account-deletion-30d", invoicesMinimised }, now)`,
+  where `kinds` lists the kinds erased (`account`, `sessions`, `events`,
+  `tickets`, `subscriber`, `invoice.email`, `invoice.phone`,
+  `invoice.userId`) and `invoicesMinimised` is a count. It holds no invoice
+  ids, because those next to the userId would restore the link.
+- Invoice purge writes one entry per invoice:
+  `record("invoice.purged", invoiceId, { kinds: ["billing"], rule: "invoice-retention-7y" }, now)`.
+- On erasure, `detail.userId` is removed from the `invoice.issued` entries
+  of the account's invoices.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- The audit log is edited in one place, which is the removal of a copied
+  link. No entry is added or removed by that edit.
+- The erased userId stays as the subject of the account's audit entries.
+  With the account record gone and every other copy erased, it identifies
+  no one.

+# Account erasure
+
+When a customer deletes their account, erase their personal data within 30
+days, but keep their invoices for 7 years for tax.
+
+Decisions: [erase at deletion](adr/0001-erase-at-deletion.md),
+[invoice minimisation and retention](adr/0002-invoice-minimisation-and-retention.md),
+[erasure audit entry](adr/0003-erasure-audit-entry.md).
+Contracts: [account erasure](spec/account-erasure.md),
+[invoice retention purge](spec/invoice-retention-purge.md).
+
+## Where personal data lives today
+
+All data is held in memory in `db` (`src/store.js`). It resets on restart, so
+no account soft-deleted before this change outlives a restart and nothing
+needs migrating.
+
+| Store | Personal data | Written by | On delete today | Confidence |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `db.users` | name, email, phone, address | `createAccount`, `updateProfile` (`src/accounts.js`) | flagged with `deletedAt`, **kept** | observed |
+| `db.sessions` | userId, email | `signIn` (`src/accounts.js`) | deleted | observed |
+| `db.invoices` | `billing.{name, email, phone, address, taxId}`, `userId` | `issueInvoice` (`src/invoices.js`) | **kept, unchanged** | observed |
+| `db.tickets` | userId, email, free-text subject and body | `openTicket` (`src/support.js`) | **kept** | observed |
+| `db.events` | userId, email, props | `track` (`src/analytics.js`), including `DELETE /me` itself (`src/server.js:44`) just before deleting | **kept**, and deletion adds one more | observed |
+| `db.subscribers` | email (the key), name | `subscribe` (`src/newsletter.js`), keyed by email, no userId, not called by any route today | **kept** | observed; the match to the account is by the account email (inferred) |
+| `db.audit` | userId as subject; `invoice.issued` carries `detail.userId`, a copy of the invoice→account link; `account.updated` stores field names only | `record` (`src/audit.js`) | kept | observed |
+
+No logging exists beyond the startup port line, and error messages carry no
+personal data (observed).
+
+Gap: a newsletter signup made with a different email address cannot be tied
+to the account and is out of reach of this change (inferred).
+
+## Steps
+
+Riskiest first. `npm test` is the check for every step.
+
+1. **Thin path through the invoice/user boundary.** Add `eraseAccount` in
+   `src/erasure.js` covering sessions, the `db.users` entry, invoice
+   minimisation and the `account.erased` audit entry, and call it from
+   `deleteAccount`. Remove `deletedAt` and its checks.
+   Done when a new `test/erasure.test.js` shows that after deletion
+   `db.users` has no entry for the account. The account's invoice must still
+   have name, address, taxId, lines, total and issuedAt, and must have no
+   email, phone or userId. There must be exactly one `account.erased` entry,
+   and it must contain none of the account's values. The existing
+   `test/accounts.test.js` and `test/server.test.js` must still pass.
+2. **Remaining copies.** Extend `eraseAccount` to events, tickets, the
+   newsletter subscriber and the `invoice.issued` audit link, and remove the
+   `track(user, "account.delete_requested")` call from `DELETE /me`.
+   Done when a test that goes through `DELETE /me` finds no event, ticket,
+   subscriber or `invoice.issued` `detail.userId` left for the account, and
+   a second account's data in every store is unchanged.
+3. **Retention purge.** Add `purgeExpiredInvoices` to `dailyJobs`.
+   Done when tests show three cases. An erased invoice 7 years minus a day
+   past issue is kept. One 7 years plus a day past issue is deleted, with an
+   `invoice.purged` audit entry. A live account's invoice 8 years past issue
+   is kept.
+
+## Done
+

+# 0002 Invoice minimisation and retention
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted.
+
+## Context
+
+Invoices are tax records and must be kept for 7 years from their issue date
+with their line items, amounts, and the billing name, address and tax id.
+`issueInvoice` also copies the customer's email and phone into `billing` and
+keeps `userId`, none of which tax requires.
+
+## Decision
+
+On erasure, each invoice of the account:
+
+- **keeps** `id`, `issuedAt`, `lines`, `total`, `billing.name`,
+  `billing.address`, `billing.taxId`;
+- **drops** `billing.email` and `billing.phone`, and sets `userId` to `null`;
+- **gains** `erasedAt` (ISO timestamp of the erasure).
+
+When an invoice has `erasedAt` set and its `issuedAt` plus 7 calendar years
+is before now, a daily job deletes it
+([spec](../spec/invoice-retention-purge.md)). The retained billing name and
+address are personal data kept only under the tax exception, which ends at
+that point.
+
+Invoices of live accounts are not touched by either rule.
+
+## Consequences
+
+- `invoicesFor(userId)` returns nothing for an erased account. That is
+  intended, because no account is left to ask.
+- Retained invoices stay readable by id in `db.invoices`.

+import { test, beforeEach } from "node:test"
+import assert from "node:assert/strict"
+import { reset, db } from "../src/store.js"
+import { createAccount, deleteAccount, findAccount, signIn, userForToken } from "../src/accounts.js"
+import { invoicesFor, issueInvoice } from "../src/invoices.js"
+import { openTicket, ticketsFor } from "../src/support.js"
+import { eventsFor, track } from "../src/analytics.js"
+import { isSubscribed, subscribe } from "../src/newsletter.js"
+import { createServer } from "../src/server.js"
+
+beforeEach(reset)
+
+const ada = { name: "Ada Park", email: "ada@studio.example", phone: "+44 20 7946 0000", address: "1 Loom Lane, London" }
+const lines = [{ description: "Brand workshop", quantity: 2, unitPrice: 45000 }]
+
+// Everything any store holds for one account, copied so later changes show up in a comparison.
+function storedFor(user) {
+  return structuredClone({
+    account: findAccount(user.id),
+    sessions: [...db.sessions.values()].filter((session) => session.userId === user.id),
+    invoices: invoicesFor(user.id),
+    tickets: ticketsFor(user.id),
+    events: eventsFor(user.id),
+    subscriber: db.subscribers.get(user.email),
+    audit: db.audit.filter((entry) => entry.subject === user.id || entry.detail.userId === user.id),
+  })
+}
+
+test("deleting an account removes its record and sessions", () => {
+  const user = createAccount(ada)
+  signIn(ada.email)
+  deleteAccount(user.id)
+  assert.equal(db.users.has(user.id), false)
+  assert.equal(db.sessions.size, 0)
+})
+
+test("an erased account's invoice keeps its tax fields and loses the rest", () => {
+  const user = createAccount(ada)
+  const issued = issueInvoice(user.id, lines, { taxId: "GB123456789" })
+  const kept = structuredClone(issued)
+  deleteAccount(user.id)
+  const invoice = db.invoices.get(issued.id)
+  assert.equal(invoice.issuedAt, kept.issuedAt)
+  assert.deepEqual(invoice.lines, kept.lines)
+  assert.equal(invoice.total, kept.total)
+  assert.deepEqual(invoice.billing, { name: ada.name, address: ada.address, taxId: "GB123456789" })
+  assert.equal(invoice.userId, null)
+  assert.ok(invoice.erasedAt)
+})
+
+test("erasure writes one audit entry that holds none of the account's values", () => {
+  const user = createAccount(ada)
+  const invoice = issueInvoice(user.id, lines, { taxId: "GB123456789" })
+  deleteAccount(user.id)
+  const entries = db.audit.filter((entry) => entry.action === "account.erased")
+  assert.equal(entries.length, 1)
+  assert.equal(entries[0].subject, user.id)
+  assert.equal(entries[0].detail.rule, "account-deletion-30d")
+  assert.equal(entries[0].detail.invoicesMinimised, 1)
+  const written = JSON.stringify(entries[0])
+  for (const value of [ada.name, ada.email, ada.phone, ada.address, "GB123456789", invoice.id]) {
+    assert.equal(written.includes(value), false, `audit entry leaks ${value}`)
+  }
